prompt:

Seat her on a low, solid rectangular wooden artist's seat (a simple box-shaped seat with no exposed chair legs). Adjust her seated body angle naturally to a front-side three-quarter view so both legs can be followed separately. Exactly TWO thighs emerge from the shorts, each leads to its own visible knee, then its own lower leg descending toward the floor, then one ankle and one bare foot. Both feet rest flat on the paint-covered floor cloth, a small clear gap between the ankles and feet. Both knees bend comfortably over the seat edge. No leg folds behind or underneath her hips, no crossed legs, no hidden extra calf under another leg. Replace all old flesh-shaped remnants below the legs with ordinary flat paint-stained cloth and floor. Keep the feet naturally proportioned with five toes each.
Make the pelvis and torso align comfortably with this new seated pose; retain her face, hairstyle, outfit and brush-sorting activity. Exactly two connected arms, two hands, two connected legs and two feet total. Keep hair and loose shirt fabric away from the knees and ankles so the two leg chains remain readable.

Full-body vertical portrait at 1024x1536, with the complete head, hands and both feet inside the frame. Same glossy illustration style, one woman, no new people, no armor, no text or watermark.
